findings.title: Used recovery codes are never invalidated when credential lives in user storage
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login the authenticator now looks the credential up via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which may return a credential coming from getFederatedCredentialsStream() (i.e. built on the fly by the user-storage provider). For such a credential nothing is written back: the code is not marked as used and only removeStoredCredentialById() is attempted when all codes are used — that call operates on local (Keycloak DB) credentials and the federated model may even have a null id, so it is a no-op. Consequently a single recovery code stored in user storage can be reused indefinitely, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never triggered after exhaustion. Some write-back path (e.g. updateCredential with the consumed code removed) is needed.

findings.title: Login form always asks for recovery code #0 for federated credentials / unchecked Optional.get()
findings.body: codeNumber is derived from getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() of a credential model that, for user-storage backed users, is reconstructed fresh from the provider on every request with no usage state. The form therefore always prompts for the first code, which combined with the missing invalidation makes the flow effectively single-code. Additionally credentialModelOpt.get() is called without isPresent() check, so if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns empty the page rendering fails with NoSuchElementException instead of a meaningful error.

findings.title: getCredentials() can NPE when user is not in the in-memory map
findings.body: getMyUser(user) returns null for any user whose username is not present in the `users` map (e.g. a local-storage user or a stale cached federated reference), and the very next line dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. Other methods in this class (isConfiguredFor, isValid, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) all guard against null. This will throw a NullPointerException from credential enumeration paths (account console / admin REST) and break tests.

findings.title: Recovery-codes credential returned from getCredentials() has no id
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) does not carry over myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(), so the returned CredentialModel has a null id. Callers such as RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator use getId() for removeStoredCredentialById and the account REST API exposes credential ids, so a null id leads to silent no-ops or confusing responses.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are handed to user storage as plaintext JSON with no documented contract
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the full list of raw (unhashed) recovery codes into UserCredentialModel.challengeResponse and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Any user-storage provider implementing CredentialInputUpdater now receives all recovery codes in clear text, whereas local storage stores only hashes (the test provider in this PR indeed stores and compares them in plaintext). At minimum the hashing/storage expectation must be documented on this public helper, and ideally hashed values (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode) should be passed instead.
